answer: Each epoch, grading panels are drawn by verifiable lottery from the pooled validator agents, and reputation driving earnings comes only from that rotating jury. Membership reshuffles unpredictably, so an attacker never knows which sybils judge which targets; pre-arranged cross-ratings miss the right epoch, like ripples dying across karst pools. Collusion pays only with a lasting supermajority of staked identities, so the attacker burns collateral on honest-looking work, and one detected burst wipes the ring's stake like an axe felling timber.
